name: SiteLayout
label: Site layout
description: The frame of a docs or marketing site: header, sidebar, content, aside and footer, with the page's width and the sidebar's dock set apart.

props.name: children
props.description: The page's main content: the article, the page.

props.name: header
props.description:
The top bar, usually a SiteHeader. A SiteHeader given no `width` of its
own follows `headerWidth`, so the bar lines up with the page below it.

props.name: sidebar
props.description:
The navigation column, usually a scrollable NavList: the wide-screen
form of the site's sub-navigation. Sticks below the header; below
960px it leaves the page, and the header's own menu carries the same
pages (give each SiteHeader section its `drawerItems`), so a reader has
one menu, never two.

props.name: aside
props.description: The column after the content, usually an AnchorNav reading the page's headings. Gives way below 1152px in the `column` placement.

props.name: asidePlacement
props.description:
Where the aside sits. `column` gives it a column of its own after the
content. `edge` pins it to the window's end edge, centred on the
height, and gives the content the room: the place for AnchorNav's
`floating` variant, a minimap that opens on hover or focus. Hidden
below 960px in either.

props.name: footer
props.description: The bottom of the site, usually a SiteFooter.

props.name: width
props.description:
How wide the page runs, the shell recipe's width axis. `contained`
centres the columns at the contained width (1440px, or the nearest
`--ds-shell-contained-width`); `full` runs them edge to edge, the side
gutter aside.

props.name: containedWidth
props.description:
The contained width's step, for a page a level narrower or wider than
the default: `narrow` (1200px, a 1080px article beside an edge-docked sidebar), `default` (1440px) or `wide` (1680px).
The header and the footer follow it when contained. With the sidebar
docked to the edge, the step caps the room after the sidebar; docked to
the content, it caps the sidebar and the content together.

props.name: headerWidth
props.description:
How wide the header's bar runs, for a SiteHeader that sets no `width`
of its own. It moves with the sidebar's dock: `full` when the sidebar
docks to the window's edge (so the brand sits over the sidebar, flush
with the same edge), the page's `width` when it docks beside the
content. Set it only to break that pairing.

props.name: footerWidth
props.description:
How wide the footer's row runs. It moves with the header: `full` when
the sidebar docks to the window's edge, the page's `width` when it
docks beside the content, so the top and the bottom of the site always
agree. Set it only to break that pairing.

props.name: sidebarDock
props.description:
Where the sidebar sits. `content` keeps it in the page's row, beside the
content, so a contained page centres all three columns together. `edge`
docks it to the window's start edge behind a hairline, and the content
and aside are laid out (and contained) in the room after it.

props.name: readingWidth
props.description:
Hold the main column to a reading width (about 75 characters of body
text, centred in its column) while the page is contained. A full-width page lets the content run the whole column.
`--ds-site-layout-reading-width` sets the measure.

props.name: mainId
props.description: The id of the main region, the skip link's target.

props.name: skipLinkLabel
props.description: The skip link's text, the page's first stop. Pass an empty string for none.

props.name: sidebarLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the sidebar's navigation landmark.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the aside's complementary landmark.

keys.note: A frame: its slots own their keys, and its skip link is a native link.

alternatives.name: AppLayout
alternatives.when: the page is an app screen with a rail of tools rather than a site of pages
